# Sirach Chapter 40 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_040_page_001.jpg

---

40:1 Much toil has been allotted to every human being, and a heavy yoke lies upon the sons of Adam from the day they come forth from their mother's womb until the day they return to the mother of all the living.

40:2 Perplexity and fear of heart, anxious anticipation and the day of death —

40:3 from the one enthroned in glory to the one laid low in dust and ashes,

40:4 from the one arrayed in purple and a crown to the one wrapped in coarse linen —

40:5 there is wrath and envy and trouble and restlessness and fear of death and rage and conflict. And when someone lies down on his bed to rest, his sleep at night confuses his mind.

40:6 He gets little or no rest; as in a day's watch he is disturbed in his sleep: sometimes tormented by a terrifying dream, sometimes sinking into drowsiness with just a moment of relief — as if rescued from the day of battle.

40:7 He wakes up in astonishment that the terror amounted to nothing.

40:8 All creatures experience such things — human beings and animals — but for sinners they increase sevenfold.

40:9 Death and bloodshed and strife and sword, disasters, famine and ruin and plague —

40:10 all these were made for the wicked, and the Flood came because of them.

40:11 Everything that comes from the earth returns to the earth, and what comes from the waters returns to the sea.

40:12 All bribery and injustice will be wiped away, but faithfulness will endure forever.

40:13 The wealth of an unjust person dries up like a wadi, and vanishes like a violent thunderclap.

40:14 A generous person will rejoice, but transgressors will come to total ruin.

40:15 The offspring of the godless will not put forth many branches, and unclean roots stand on crumbling rock.

40:16 The reeds along any riverbank are uprooted before all other grass.

40:17 Kindness is like a garden of delight, and almsgiving endures forever.

40:18 The life of a self-sufficient laborer is sweet, but better than both is one who finds a treasure.

40:19 Children and the founding of a city preserve a name, but better than both is one who finds wisdom. Livestock and orchards make a person prosperous, but better than both is a wife whom one loves.

40:20 Wine and music bring joy to the heart, but better than both is the love of wisdom.

40:21 The flute and the lyre make pleasant sound, but better than both is a lovely voice.

40:22 The eye longs for grace and beauty, but better than both are the green shoots of new grain.

40:23 A friend and a companion are welcome at any time, but better than both is a wife together with her husband.

40:24 Kinsfolk and helpers are for times of trouble, but charity delivers more effectively than either.

40:25 Gold and silver give a firm footing, but better than either is good counsel.

40:26 Riches and strength give confidence, but better than either is the fear of the Lord. In the fear of the Lord there is no want, and there is no need to look for any other support.

40:27 The fear of the Lord is a garden full of blessing, and it covers one with more glory than any canopy.

40:28 My child, do not live the life of a beggar; it is better to die than to beg.

40:29 When a person looks to another's table for sustenance, that existence cannot truly be called a life. One defiles oneself with another's food, but the intelligent and well-educated person avoids this.

40:30 In the mouth of the shameless, begging tastes sweet, but it sets a fire burning in his stomach.
